findings.source_passage: West Egg, especially, still figures in my more fantastic dreams. I see it as a night scene by El Greco: a hundred houses, at once conventional and grotesque, crouching under a sullen, overhanging sky
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Even when the East excited me most'
findings.why_it_matters: The El Greco vision of West Egg is one of the novel's most critically discussed passages—a set-piece of Gothic distortion that concretizes Nick's thesis about Eastern unreality and the Westerners' unadaptability. It carries heavy interpretive weight and is prosodically distinctive. The draft jumps from 'quality of distortion' directly to 'After Gatsby's death the East was haunted,' erasing the entire tableau.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the El Greco passage verbatim: 'West Egg, especially, still figures in my more fantastic dreams. I see it as a night scene by El Greco: a hundred houses, at once conventional and grotesque…Gravely the men turn in at a house—the wrong house. But no one knows the woman's name, and no one cares.' This is non-negotiable signature prose.

findings.source_passage: They were careless people, Tom and Daisy—they smashed up things and creatures and then retreated back into their money or their vast carelessness, or whatever it was that kept them together, and let other people clean up the mess they had made
findings.source_locator: paragraph after Tom's confession on Fifth Avenue
findings.why_it_matters: This is present verbatim in the draft—no finding here. (Checking this as a control.)

findings.source_passage: That's my Middle West—not the wheat or the prairies or the lost Swede towns, but the thrilling returning trains of my youth, and the street lamps and sleigh bells in the frosty dark
findings.why_it_matters: The draft substitutes 'one of my most vivid memories is of coming back West at Christmas time—the thrilling returning trains of my youth, and the street lamps and sleigh bells in the frosty dark,' cutting the rhetorically crucial 'That's my Middle West—not the wheat or the prairies or the lost Swede towns' declaration and the full Union Station evocation. The sentence 'That's my Middle West' is a widely recognized voice-signature that defines Nick's Midwestern identity and the novel's central 'story of the West' thesis; its loss flattens the interpretive pivot.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the declarative 'That's my Middle West—not the wheat or the prairies or the lost Swede towns, but…' sentence as the opening of that paragraph. The authorized cut covers the Union Station travelogue but not this thesis sentence.

findings.source_locator: After the funeral, Owl Eyes speaks to Nick by the gate
findings.why_it_matters: Owl Eyes's epitaph 'The poor son-of-a-bitch' is culturally famous, widely anthologized, and critically returned to as the novel's most bracingly honest eulogy—the one mourner who sees Gatsby plainly. The exchange 'they used to go there by the hundreds' / 'The poor son-of-a-bitch' is entirely absent from the draft. Although Owl Eyes is an authorized minor-character removal, this specific line is a signature that the cuts inventory does not authorize erasing—it can be delivered without naming Owl Eyes.
findings.suggested_fix: Even with Owl Eyes cut as a named character, preserve the moment: an unnamed voice at the graveside who says 'The poor son-of-a-bitch.' The line is too famous and too interpretively loaded to drop silently.

findings.source_passage: She showed a surprising amount of character about it too—looked at the coroner with determined eyes under that corrected brow of hers, and swore that her sister had never seen Gatsby
findings.why_it_matters: The draft omits the character detail 'She showed a surprising amount of character about it too—looked at the coroner with determined eyes under that corrected brow of hers, and cried into her handkerchief, as if the very suggestion was more than she could endure.' This ironic observation—one of Fitzgerald's sharpest social-satirical asides—establishes the novel's mordant tone about how the powerful and adjacent-powerful cover up their crimes. The draft preserves the bare fact of Catherine's testimony but loses the voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'She showed a surprising amount of character about it too—looked at the coroner with determined eyes under that corrected brow of hers, and swore…and cried into her handkerchief, as if the very suggestion was more than she could endure.' This is compact and can be inserted without word-count penalty.

findings.source_passage: I felt suddenly as though I were talking to a child. Then he went into the jewellery store to buy a pearl necklace—or perhaps only a pair of cuff buttons—rid of my provincial squeamishness forever.
findings.source_locator: End of the Tom Buchanan Fifth Avenue encounter
findings.why_it_matters: The closing image of Tom buying jewelry—the ironic finality of 'rid of my provincial squeamishness forever'—is Nick's definitive moral verdict on Tom and on his own departure from Eastern values. The draft ends the scene with '…let other people clean up the mess they had made…' and moves on, losing the rhetorical sting of the closing clause that critics cite as Nick's formal severance from the East.
findings.suggested_fix: Add after the handshake: 'I felt suddenly as though I were talking to a child. Then he went into the jewellery store to buy a pearl necklace—or perhaps only a pair of cuff buttons—rid of my provincial squeamishness forever.' This is the scene's earned closing irony.

findings.source_passage: his protest continued in my brain: 'Look here, old sport, you've got to get somebody for me. You've got to try hard. I can't go through this alone.'
findings.source_locator: After Nick returns to the drawing-room, unable to reach Wolfshiem
findings.why_it_matters: This interior monologue—Gatsby's imagined voice haunting Nick in death—is one of the most pathos-laden moments in the chapter and the novel. The phrase 'old sport' in a context of abandonment is a tonal and thematic signature. The draft omits it entirely, moving from the failed phone call directly to the next morning's letter.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the imagined voice passage: 'I went back to the drawing-room and thought for an instant that they were chance visitors… his protest continued in my brain: Look here, old sport, you've got to get somebody for me. You've got to try hard. I can't go through this alone.'

summary: The draft commits one unambiguous high-severity loss (the El Greco / West Egg vision, a critically canonical passage), one high-severity near-miss on a thesis sentence ('That's my Middle West'), and four medium-severity losses including the erasure of 'The poor son-of-a-bitch,' Gatsby's haunting 'old sport' voice in death, Tom's ironic jewelry-store exit, and Catherine's character detail—together requiring regeneration.
